title: かたつむり (Katatsumuri — Snail)
description: A playful 1911 elementary school song asking a snail: 'Where is your head? Where are your eyes?' — prompting it to extend its tentacles. The song connects to a classic kyogen (traditional comedy) play about a snail, and has been used in Japanese schools for over a century. Very simple vocabulary and a catchy, repetitive structure make it perfect for beginners learning body part vocabulary. One of the best-known 文部省唱歌 (Ministry of Education songs), published in the first volume of 尋常小学唱歌. Children still sing it while playing with snails during Japan's rainy season (梅雨).
